note: A room-grain COMMUNITY VOCABULARY is under design on main (brainstorm only, no branch, no writes): biome decomposed into independently-valued axes - physiognomy, energy, water, substrate, light, disturbance - shared between cell grain and room grain, so that a taiga and a gallery forest and a fungal mangrove are points in one space rather than three atoms. THREE OVERLAPS WITH LIVE WORK, all found by reading, none acted on. (1) The Rill Task 5 grounds MicroField.wetness as a budget-and-allocation: cell-scale moisture redistributed by position relative to the local watercourse. That is exactly the pattern this design proposes for EVERY axis. The Rill gets there first and should; the axes work generalizes it rather than competing. (2) MicroField already carries FOUR room-grain axes - relief, aspect, wetness, openness - drawn as pure noise off LOCALE_MICRO and consulting the world for none of them. openness IS canopy closure and aspect drives light, so three of the four are ungrounded axes of that same vocabulary. Grounding one must keep its draw and spend it as variation about the grounded value, per the save-format note in The Rill Task 5. (3) The Grain thesis, that the fine layer should vary, is the same rung one campaign earlier. FOUR FREE FINDINGS, unrelated to any of that, offered to whoever wants them: is_marine is a two-realm partition and not-is_marine silently means land in provider.rs and in graph_derive.rs, so an underdark biome would be counted as land in the connection graph; vantage.rs treats any stratum other than Surface as submerged, so a cave chamber would tell the client the player is underwater; SoilOrder is derived in terrain lithology and read by nothing in the biome path, which is the edaphic axis sitting unused; and the guard an_addresss_meaning_does_not_depend_on_which_other_chambers_exist uses two Karst fixtures, so it varies depth while holding cave kind fixed and would stay green and vacuous against any change that makes chamber content read CaveKind.
